'''Daniela Kühn''' {{post-nominals|FRS}} (born 1973)<ref>Birth year from [http://www.isni.org/isni/0000000016376126 ISNI authority control file], retrieved 2018-11-28.</ref> is a German mathematician and an Emeritus Professor and former Mason Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Birmingham]] in Birmingham, England.<ref name="profile">[https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/staff/profiles/maths/honorary-staff/kuhn-daniela Staff profile], University of Birmingham School of Mathematics, accessed 2026-09-13.</ref> She is known for her research in [[combinatorics]], and particularly in [[extremal combinatorics]] and [[graph theory]].

==Biography==
Kühn earned the [[Part III of the Mathematical Tripos|Certificate of Advanced Studies in Mathematics]] ([[Cambridge Mathematical Tripos]]) from [[Cambridge University]] in 1997 and a Diploma in Mathematics from the [[Chemnitz University of Technology]] in 1999,<ref name="profile"/> followed by her doctorate from the [[University of Hamburg]] in 2001, under the supervision of [[Reinhard Diestel]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=78181}}</ref> After working as a postdoctoral researcher at Hamburg and the [[Free University of Berlin]], she moved to the [[University of Birmingham]] as a lecturer in 2004, and was awarded the [[Mason Professorship]] of Mathematics in 2010.<ref name="profile"/>

==Research==
In 2004 Kühn published a pair of papers in ''[[Combinatorica]]'' with her thesis advisor, Reinhard Diestel, concerning the [[cycle space]]s of infinite graphs. In these graphs the appropriate generalizations of [[cycle (graph theory)|cycles]] and [[spanning tree]]s hinge on a proper treatment of the [[end (graph theory)|ends]] of the graph. Reviewer [[R. Bruce Richter]] writes that "the results are extremely satisfactory, in the sense that standard theorems for finite graphs have perfect analogues" but that "there is nothing simple about any aspect of this work. It is a nice mix of graph-theoretic and topological ideas."<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Diestel | first1 = Reinhard
 | last2 = Kühn | first2 = Daniela
 | doi = 10.1007/s00493-004-0005-z
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Combinatorica
 | mr = 2057684
 | pages = 69–89 & 91–116
 | title = On infinite cycles. I, II.
 | volume = 24
 | year = 2004| s2cid = 15797002
 }}. See in particular Richter's review in the MR link.</ref>

In 2011, Kühn and her co-authors published a proof of [[Sumner's conjecture]], that "every ''n''-vertex [[polytree]] forms a subgraph of every (2''n''&nbsp;&minus;&nbsp;2)-vertex [[tournament]]", for all but finitely many values of&nbsp;''n''. [[MathSciNet]] reviewer K. B. Reid wrote that their proof "is an important and welcome development in tournament theory".<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Kühn | first1 = Daniela
 | last2 = Mycroft | first2 = Richard
 | last3 = Osthus | first3 = Deryk
 | arxiv = 1010.4430
 | doi = 10.1112/plms/pdq035
 | issue = 4
 | journal = [[Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society]] | series = Third Series
 | mr = 2793448 | zbl=1218.05034
 | pages = 731–766
 | title = A proof of Sumner's universal tournament conjecture for large tournaments
 | volume = 102
 | year = 2011| s2cid = 119169562
 }}.</ref>

==Awards and honours==
In 2002, Kühn won the Richard Rado Prize, a biennial best dissertation award given by the Section for Discrete Mathematics of the [[German Mathematical Society]].<ref>[https://www3.math.tu-berlin.de/dm/radopreis.html Richard-Rado-Preis] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130106114013/https://www3.math.tu-berlin.de/dm/radopreis.html |date=2013-01-06 }} (in German), Fachgruppe Diskrete Mathematik, DMV, accessed 2012-09-12.</ref> Together with [[Deryk Osthus]] and Alain Plagne, she was one of the first winners of the [[European Prize in Combinatorics]] in 2003.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ems-ph.org/journals/newsletter/pdf/2003-12-50.pdf|journal=European Mathematical Society Newsletter|date=December 2003|volume=50|page=24|title=Awards}}.</ref> Together with Osthus, she was a recipient of the 2014 [[Whitehead Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] for "their many results in extremal graph theory and related areas. Several of their papers resolve long-standing open problems in the area."<ref>{{cite web|title=LMS Prizes 2014|url=https://www.lms.ac.uk/prizes/lms-prizes-2013|publisher=London Mathematical Society|accessdate=7 August 2014}}</ref> She was an Invited Speaker at the 2014 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], in [[Seoul]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers since 1897|url = http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|website = International Mathematical Union (IMU)|accessdate = 2015-09-27|date = 2015-09-27|archive-date = 2017-11-08|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171108012153/http://www.mathunion.org/db/ICM/Speakers/SortedByCongress.php|url-status = dead}}</ref> and appointed as a [[Royal Society]] [[Wolfson Research Merit Award]] holder in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Royal Society announces recipients of prestigious Wolfson Research Merit Awards|url = https://royalsociety.org/news/2015/07/wolfson-research-merit-awards-july/|website = Royal Society|accessdate = 2015-09-27|date = 31 July 2015}}</ref> She was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Daniela Kühn FRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/daniela-k%c3%bchn-36726/ |access-date=2024-05-20 |website=Royal Society |language=en}}</ref>
